newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Put spreads seen in OEX and SPX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Put spreads seen in OEX and SPX.

text.p: The U.S. stock market's strong rally did not drive investors to index calls, as some of the biggest trades were put spreads in the S&P 100 index .OEX and the S&P 500 .SPX, traders said Tuesday.

In the OEX, the June 720/735 put spread traded about 5,000 times. In the SPX, the July 880/June 750 put spread traded in a one-by-two, with the July 800 trading about 600 contracts and the June 750 about 1,200.
By about 1100 CDT/1600 GMT, the bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI was up 106 points at 6,889, just off its 6,897 session high.
Among the broader indices, the OEX was up 14 points at about 770 and the SPX gained 14 to 787. June S&P 500 futures were up 15.55 at 790.75.
"Out-of-the money calls really haven't done anything," one trader in SPX options said. "Call volatility dropped and the put (volatility) is slightly on the rise."
Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX, said call buying was light and there appeared to be more interest in the puts.
He said a customer bought the June OEX put spread.
"Everybody's sitting here waiting for the next number," he said, referring to forthcoming economic reports.
The first quarter employment cost index, reported before the market opened Tuesday, was lower than expected and was the driving force behind the market's sharp gains, traders said.
"This was the number they were looking at," the SPX options trader said of the employment cost index. "Friday's the next big number, but I think this had more a weight factor on the market."
U.S. April employment figures are due Friday.
"I really do expect Friday's number to be a non-event," he said. "It might be built up, but it won't be a big event."
In the May series, trading was fairly even between the puts and the calls, with no large orders and no big directional plays, he added.
Callahan said the one sure bet is that volatility will remain high through the week.
"This is a volatile market, so expect more of the same," he said. "We're still in the early stages of it."
Among May SPX options, the May 785 call traded about 3,450 and the 770 put traded about 3,125.
In the OEX, the May 740 put was the most active front-month option, with turnover of nearly 4,800 contracts. The May 765 call traded about 4,600.
